case_title: Deepak Gulati v. State of Haryana
evidence_type: Testimonial (prosecutrix's court deposition and Section 164 statement; father's and investigating officer's deposition); medical officer's deposition; school register proving age; hostile warden's deposition
mitigating_circumstances: Appellant had already served more than 3 years of sentence; the victim was 19, left home voluntarily and made no complaint during the period of intimacy
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC ss.365 and 376; RI 3 years and Rs.2,000 fine (s.365); RI 7 years and Rs.5,000 fine (s.376); sentences concurrent
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentences affirmed
neutral_facts: The victim, a 19-year-old student, had known the accused for some time, and the accused had been meeting her outside her school in an attempt to develop intimate relations. On the day in question the accused induced the victim to travel with him to Kurukshetra so that they could get married, and she agreed. En route, the accused took her to a lake, where, according to the prosecution, he had sexual intercourse with her against her wishes, behind bushes. He then took her to Kurukshetra, where she stayed with his relatives for three or four days, during which he allegedly raped her. The accused later threw her out of the house. She went to a university hostel, where the warden became suspicious and questioned her; the victim narrated the incident and the warden informed her father. The victim later met the accused at a temple, where he allegedly persuaded her to accompany him to Ambala to marry. At the bus stand, the victim's father and police officers were present, and the accused was apprehended. The victim's father had lodged a complaint alleging enticement and wrongful confinement. The victim was medically examined, and the medical officer deposed that she had indulged in sexual intercourse and was habitual to it. Her statement was recorded before a Magistrate under Section 164 Cr.P.C. The warden, declared hostile, deposed that the victim had stayed in the hostel without permission. The school register established the victim's date of birth. The investigating officer deposed about the search and apprehension.
physical_harm: No injuries stated; medical officer deposed the victim had indulged in sexual intercourse and was habitual to it
premeditation_planning: Not found against the accused. The Court found an agreed plan to marry in court at Ambala and held there was no basis to show a false promise from the outset.
motive: alleged: the accused obtained the victim's consent to sexual intercourse through a false promise of marriage to satisfy his lust; the Court did not accept this allegation
key_evidence_accepted: The victim's own account, read with the undisputed facts: she left home voluntarily to marry, stayed with the accused, was intimate with him voluntarily, and was apprehended with him at the bus stand; the school register showing her age
witness_credibility: Court noted material contradictions and improvements in the father's and investigating officer's evidence and omission of the lake incident in the Section 164 statement; it relied on the victim's own version as to voluntariness
post_offence_conduct: Not stated as misconduct; per the victim, the accused threw her out after about four days and later persuaded her to go to Ambala; they were apprehended together at the bus stand
custody_duration: More than 3 years of sentence served (exact custody period not stated)
bail_history: Appellant on bail at the time of the Supreme Court's decision; bail bonds discharged. Earlier bail history not stated
trial_duration: offence: 10.5.1995; trial judgment: 13.11.1998; High Court: 28.1.2010; Supreme Court: 20.5.2013
legal_representation: Amit Pawan for the appellant (no one appeared for the appellant at the hearing); Kamal Mohan Gupta for the State
investigation_status: FIR registered on complaint of 16.5.1995 (ss.365/366 IPC, later converted to ss.365/376); victim medically examined 17.5.1995; Section 164 statement recorded; chargesheet filed; charges framed 3.6.1996; 13 prosecution witnesses examined; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under ss.365 and 376 IPC. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence affirmed. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, conviction and sentence set aside
prosecution_argument: Not stated; the State's counsel assisted the Court but the judgment records no specific arguments
defence_argument: Not stated; no one appeared for the appellant, so the Court examined the record
legal_principle_applied: Consent obtained on a false promise of marriage amounts to rape only if the accused had no intention to marry from the outset (mala fide intent and clandestine motive); mere breach of promise is not enough; s.90 IPC applies only where the accused never intended to marry; s.114-A Evidence Act not attracted
precedent_relied_upon: Uday v. State of Karnataka, AIR 2003 SC 1639; Deelip Singh @ Dilip Kumar v. State of Bihar, AIR 2005 SC 203; Yedla Srinivasa Rao v. State of A.P., (2006) 11 SCC 615; Pradeep Kumar Verma v. State of Bihar & Anr., AIR 2007 SC 3059; N. Jaladu, Re ILR (1913) 36 Mad 453
sentencing_rationale: Not applicable (acquittal on benefit of doubt)
judicial_mitigating_factors: Appellant had already served more than 3 years of sentence
